detailed_description:
[Shot 1] 00:00-00:15, one uninterrupted wide front-three-quarter shot. Frame one matches <Picture 2>. Start in the middle of the existing playing motion: the incoming weight transfer, right-wrist stroke, coat and camera drift continue immediately. The initial left boot is forward, right boot behind, guitar across waist with its short neck angled upward. No new introduction, pause, testing note or pose reset.
Camera remains on the same low audience-front rail, with modest lateral travel and visible pillar parallax. Keep its distance to show head, both boots, hands and all Nevan tips. Retreat slightly before the overhead movement so there is ample clear air above the entire prop. Keep the prop's front and hand contacts readable; no approach, close-up, compensating full orbit or hidden cut. Same space and light throughout.
00:00-00:03: Continue the fast existing guitar phrase, alternating actual RIGHT wrist strokes at the compact strings while LEFT fingers change fingering on the same short thick neck. Complete the incoming step and widen the grounded stance. Dante looks from strings toward the headpiece and grins slightly, enjoying control of the new instrument. Fabric follows the step.
00:03-00:06: Both hands raise the unchanged rigid Nevan out IN FRONT and ABOVE his forehead, then return it to the front waist position in one broad energetic outside arc. The guitar's flat face stays sufficiently angled toward camera to retain its recognizable blade silhouette, original dark hardware and compact neck. Its blades travel through visible free space outside head, hair, arms and coat. Knees counterbalance the motion; shoulders turn a quarter to the side with planted steps and return front. The coat trails the body. No replay of the behind-head rest or full back-facing turn.
00:06-00:10: Play the last front-facing solo phrase on the same original strings. A supported torso back lean grows from bent knees and grounded rear boot; the body then returns forward, preparing to kneel. Right wrist keeps articulating the riff, left glove stays on the original short neck. Nevan remains the exact dark violet-blue bladed design from <Picture 1>, not a newly designed electric guitar.
00:10-00:13: Dante bends through hips and BOTH knees, bringing BOTH kneecaps onto the stage, then BOTH shins settle on the floor behind him with both feet behind the hips. He decelerates into a short controlled two-knee slide, chest upright above both knees. Strike one final chord as the knees meet the floor. Nevan remains outside chest and thighs, supported by LEFT glove and the right hand during the stroke. Cloth responds after floor contact; preserve real weight and clear prop support.
00:13-00:15: Upright on both knees with both lower legs behind, Dante lets the final chord ring. The left glove holds Nevan diagonally along the left side beside the thigh; the RIGHT arm opens after the final stroke into the theatrical finishing flourish. He lifts his chest, breathes and looks forward with playful satisfaction. Hair and coat continue to settle through the last frame, with natural subtle camera travel, not a frozen image or another riff.
